options.content:
Ignite's leader controls Kafka `retention.bytes` for the **latent** and **contemporary** topic families so each family's replica-log bytes stay under a configured **allowance on every broker**. This is an approximate, reactive guard (not a filesystem quota): pressure triggers at **90%** of a broker's allowance, cleanup targets **80%**, and recovery is expected over tens of minutes as Kafka expires segments. Lowering a cap exposes old segments to Kafka's async deletion — **consumed data first**; unread data only with `RETENTION_RECLAIM_ENABLED=true`.

**How to read, in order:** 1) *Is the controller working?* (ownership + reconcile age + coverage) 2) *Which broker is under pressure?* (per-broker used vs allowance) 3) *Is cleanup happening?* (writes + unplanned reclaim) 4) *Is unread data at risk?* (state + lossy exposure). Byte values are IEC (1 GiB = 2³⁰). These metrics are leader-emitted — scope to one deployment and prefer the ownership-verified pod. Allowances cover only managed replica logs, **not total PVC use**: keep an independent disk-free alert.

panels.description: Is a leader actively running the controller? 1 = ownership verified at the last cycle entry (green); 0 = unavailable/not leader (red). A cached last-check result, not a live lease — pair with reconcile age. FIX: if 0 when management is expected, check ZooKeeper/session connectivity and that a leader is elected.
panels.title: Controller ownership

panels.description: Age of the last completed controller cycle (`time() - reconcile_timestamp`, filtered > 0 so a reset reads as no-data, not ~57 years). GOOD: below one interval (default 5m). BAD: climbing past ~15m (yellow) / 30m (red) = controller stuck, no leader, or inventory failing, so caps are no longer updated. FIX: check the Errors-by-op and ownership panels and the leader-pod logs.
panels.title: Time since last reconcile

panels.description: Controller's summary posture for the selected family. NORMAL (green) = no broker at the 90% trigger and no estimated shedding; AT_CAPACITY (orange) = at least one broker pressured; SHEDDING (red) = a resulting cap is below a partition's unread-demand estimate (loss risk, not an audit). Value 1 is retired. On incomplete inputs it may stay at its prior value. FIX: rely on the broker-pressure panels below, not this tile alone.
panels.title: State ($family)

panels.description: Did this family get a complete, trustworthy observation? 1 = broker inventory succeeded and every partition/replica was covered (green). 0 = inventory failure or a coverage gap (red) — some topics skipped and raises blocked until fresh coverage. FIX: see Errors-by-op (`describe_log_dirs`) and broker/log-dir health.
panels.title: Usage coverage ($family)

panels.description: Topics skipped this cycle because settings/offsets/coverage were unreadable. GOOD: 0. Nonzero (yellow) = some cap/backlog/state reporting may be stale for those topics (config/offset gaps don't block healthy siblings; usage gaps do). FIX: consult logs for names and Errors-by-op for the failing operation.
panels.title: Incomplete topics

panels.description: Managed topics found in the successful inventory for this family (includes idle/empty). Not a traffic rate. A sudden change indicates topic churn.
panels.title: Active topics

panels.description: Each bar = one broker's family usage as a percent of that broker's allowance (bar fills 0-100%; a broker over 100% pins full and red). GOOD: < 80% (green). WATCH: 80-90% (yellow). BAD: >= 90% (red) = pressure trigger; the controller lowers caps toward 80%. FIX: if persistently red, raise `*_RETENTION_BYTES_PER_BROKER` (needs PVC headroom) or reduce ingest; check skew across brokers.
panels.title: Broker fill % (used ÷ allowance)

panels.description: Per-broker measured family bytes (solid) against the configured per-broker allowance (dashed). GOOD: each broker's used line sits below its allowance. BAD: a used line meeting/above allowance = that broker's PVC is the one at risk. The allowance is identical across brokers; divergence in *used* is placement skew. FIX: relieve the specific broker — raise the allowance or shed load; don't average it away.
panels.title: Broker used vs allowance ($family)

panels.description: Allowance minus observed usage, per broker. GREEN = allowance headroom remaining (NOT free PVC bytes). RED (negative) = the broker is already over its family allowance and needs relief. FIX: investigate any negative broker immediately - Kafka cleanup may be pending or infeasible.
panels.title: Broker free (signed)

panels.description: Per-broker pressure flag over time (1 when used ≥ 90% of allowance). GOOD: all OK (green). BAD: PRESSURE (red) bands — correlate with the cleanup panels: pressure that persists while writes/unplanned-reclaim are active means Kafka cleanup is still catching up; pressure with no actuation needs the Errors/logs. No sticky latch: it clears when usage drops below 90%.
panels.title: Broker pressure over time

panels.description: While a broker is pressured: estimated bytes still above the 80% target under the planned caps (0 otherwise). GOOD: 0. BAD: positive and sustained = the controller cannot schedule enough relief — reclaim may be disabled, blocked by unread-data protection, or writes are failing/deferred. Zero can still coexist with pressure while Kafka cleanup is pending. Not measured freed disk. FIX: check reclaim permission, Errors-by-op and lossy-exposure panel.
panels.title: Unplanned reclaim needed (per broker)

panels.description: Successful `retention.bytes` writes per second by direction: raise (grow a finite cap), lower (shrink a finite cap), bound (replace unlimited with finite). Counts actuation, not deletion — a lower can be non-destructive. GOOD: low/steady. A burst of lower/bound during pressure is the controller reacting. FIX: sustained churn → check ingest and broker skew.
panels.title: Cap changes by direction ($family)

panels.description: A deliberately CONSERVATIVE upper bound - NOT actual unread bytes and NOT a deletion/loss measurement. Because any consumer lag protects a partition's whole retained history, this can be huge even when the real unread tail is tiny, so treat it as informational/caution history, never a paging/loss alarm. It moves only on successful lossy writes (`RETENTION_RECLAIM_ENABLED=true`) that expose retained bytes beyond the old cap; normal time-expiry is excluded. For the honest 'how close to real loss' signal use the 'Estimated unread-tail pressure' and 'Known offset gaps' panels below.
panels.title: Retained-byte bound exposed by unproven-safety (lossy) changes

panels.description: Estimated already-consumed retained bytes scheduled for reclaim by successful LOSSLESS writes - safe cleanup the controller does without permission. A flat 0 simply means no broker has needed cleanup yet (no pressure); any activity here during pressure is benign relief. The counter only exists once a lossless write has occurred. NOT a read of freed disk - verify physical usage/PVC behaviour separately.
panels.title: Consumed bytes scheduled for reclaim (estimate)

panels.description: The honest lossy-risk signal: estimated retained UNREAD-tail bytes in the worst partition divided by that partition's byte cap, per topic (only topics with complete consumption inputs and a finite cap are published; absent = unknown, NOT safe). GOOD: well below 0.8. WATCH: >= 0.8 (yellow dashed) sustained across cycles = tail approaching the cap. BAD: >= 1.0 (red dashed) = estimated unread tail at/above the cap. This is an approximation (assumes uniform bytes/offset) and is still not proof of deletion - correlate with lag, gaps and consumer health. Values are clamped to 2 for display.
panels.title: Estimated unread-tail pressure (unread ÷ cap)

panels.description: Maximum per-partition consumer lag (log end - committed) per topic, in OFFSETS - not bytes or seconds. Published only with complete consumption inputs (absent = unknown, not zero). Some lag is normal during continuous writes; investigate sustained GROWING lag together with the unread-tail ratio and gaps. Plot as a gauge/trend, not a rate.
panels.title: Consumer lag (offsets)

panels.description: Hard evidence, not estimates. 'topics w/ offset gap' = topics where the group's committed position is BELOW the retained log start (its required data is already outside the retained range) - prompt investigation (check group identity, offset resets, time-retention, reassignment/recreation); not proof THIS controller caused it. 'topics: inputs unknown' = topics whose consumption couldn't be assessed (no/err offsets, no group) - unknown is NOT caught-up. Both are 0 in the healthy case.
panels.title: Unread-risk evidence (counts)

panels.description: Per-topic observed copies for the selected family (top by on-disk bytes). Used = physical replica bytes (counts copies). Cap = per-partition `retention.bytes` × replica count; **-1 shows as Unlimited**, and segment/cleanup delay can make Used exceed Cap. Protected = conservative retained bytes that must not be evicted (any lag protects a whole partition). Unread (est) = rough offset-based backlog, reporting only. Skew = largest partition ÷ mean; high = one hot partition can hit the uniform cap. FIX: large/skewed/high-protected topics explain pressure; don't treat summed caps as reserved disk.
panels.title: Per-topic detail (top by on-disk bytes)

panels.description: The biggest consumers of the family's budget right now (observed replica bytes per object type, largest first). Use it to spot which object types dominate a pressured broker. FIX: if one or two bars dominate, that topic is the pressure driver — check its skew/protected bytes in the table.
panels.title: Top topics by on-disk bytes

panels.description: Admin-API/observation failures per second by operation (use rate, not the lifetime total). GOOD: flat 0. BAD: sustained increases — `describe_log_dirs` aborts the whole cycle; `alter_config` means caps didn't apply; `consumer_offsets` makes protection fall back to fully-protected; `leadership` blocks writes. FIX: use logs for topic names/detail; `op` legends can't be expanded into family/tenant.
panels.title: Controller errors by op

panels.description: p95 wall time of a completed controller cycle over ~1h (includes Kafka/ZooKeeper calls, planning and deliberate write-pacing — not pure CPU). GOOD: well under the configured interval (default 5m). BAD: approaching the interval = cycles can't keep up. Sparse samples are normal at a 5m cadence; no samples in a short window is not proof the controller is dead — pair with reconcile age.
panels.title: Reconcile cycle duration (p95)

panels.description: Cluster-wide sums for the family: Budget = allowance × broker count; Used = measured replica bytes across all brokers (RF>1 counts a record multiple times); Free = Budget − Used. **Diagnostic only** — a positive cluster Free cannot protect a single full broker. Always judge pressure from the per-broker panels above, never from these totals.
panels.title: Family totals (diagnostic)

panels.description: The controller's posture history for the family. GOOD: mostly NORMAL (green). AT_CAPACITY (orange) = a broker was pressured. SHEDDING (red) = estimated unread-data loss risk at that time — correlate with the lossy-exposure panel. On incomplete inputs the state can hold its previous value. This is a convenience summary; trust the per-broker pressure panels first.
panels.title: State over time ($family)

list.description: Kafka broker ID (not an Ignite pod).
list.label: Broker
list.name: broker

list.description: Filter per-topic panels to one or more objectTypes.
list.label: Object Type
list.name: objectType
